question.text: Godavari Venture Fund (Manager: Mr. Karthik Rao) was declined by an endowment LP because 'we cannot verify your thesis on the new defence-production policy — no prior track record'. Ch 12 identifies this as a classic DD challenge because:

answer.text: Newer AIFs are always riskier than established AIFs and should be avoided.
SEBI prohibits AIFs from pursuing new sectoral themes without five years of prior evidence.
Many DD points cannot be supported by tangible evidence when fundamentals are newly emerging or policy has recently changed, leading to subjective judgement that can obscure good opportunities.
Endowment LPs are not permitted to invest in first-time AIF managers under SEBI rules.

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 12 explicitly notes that newer AIFs are often avoided not because fundamentals are wrong but because not all DD points have tangible evidence — e.g., recent policy change opening a new sector. This high reliance on qualitative judgement can obscure good opportunities. The Trap: A is an overgeneralisation. B and D are fabricated rules. Cross-Exam Context: Same adverse-selection problem in XV (RA) when covering new-economy companies. In XIX-C, Managers in emerging themes (defence, space-tech, climate) should lean on policy-paper citations + advisory board signalling. Manager's Pro-Tip: For first-time or thematic funds, build a 'policy-evidence pack' — government notifications, policy-maker statements, regulatory consultations. Substitute macro evidence for missing track-record evidence.
